_: AI Debt Tracker, WEEK 5. Every number here is transcribed from the author's own saved results as published in pantry/*.svg and in narration_script.md's source table and notes. Each bar's geometry in those SVGs was recomputed as a ratio and had to agree with its printed fraction before the value was accepted. Nothing in this file is estimated, rounded for the frame, or typed from memory.

graph._geom: no bars. Node counts read off the rects: timeline 882 filings, triage 245 kept, checks 53 questions; footer 174 read + 71 reused = 245, which is the triage count exactly.

nodes.name: timeline
nodes.what: code lists every filing in the quarter's window

nodes.name: read
nodes.what: a reader runs on each kept filing, all at the same time

nodes.name: ledger
nodes.what: code merges what they found, retires matured bonds, applies the rest

nodes.name: checks
nodes.what: the graph checks its own result

graph.reused_what: readings reused by a later quarter
graph.checkpointed: Every step is checkpointed, so a stopped run picks up where it left off.
graph.stop: The run was stopped once when the laptop ran low on memory, and resumed from its checkpoints. Nothing was re-read.
graph.built_with: LangGraph: a timeline node, triage, one reader branch per relevant filing as a Send fan-out, then the ledger engine and the self-checks

engine._: what the code does with what the readers found — no model runs in this half of the graph
engine.opening_from: borrowed from the answer key — exactly the ledger B0 carries forward
engine.opening_why: With the same starting point, any difference from B0 is what reading the filings added.
engine.opening_next: Reading the opening ledger from the filings is next week.

ops.what: events from different filings that describe the same bond become one bond
bonds that have matured are retired, by the same rule B0 uses
new issues, add-ons and redemptions are applied to the opening ledger
anything it cannot place becomes an open question, never a guess

unplaceable_examples: a repayment of a bond the ledger does not hold
a new bond with no maturity
engine.cite_rule: Every change cites the passage it came from.

removed.what: bonds removed in the quarter that the tracker also removed

engine.closing_what2: What comes out is graded bond by bond against the bonds the company's own next report lists.

episodes._geom: track 260px at x=230. recall tracker 254.3/260 = 0.9781 = 97.8%; recall B0 236.3/260 = 0.9089 = 90.9%; precision tracker 234.5/260 = 0.9019 = 90.2%; precision B0 241.3/260 = 0.9281 = 92.8%. All four printed figures agree with their bar.
episodes.graded_what: development quarters graded bond by bond
episodes.same_start: both start from the same opening ledger
episodes.baseline_label: B0 · carry the last report forward

metrics.name: Bond recall
metrics.what: of the bonds the report lists, how many the ledger holds

metrics.name: Bond precision
metrics.what: of the bonds the ledger holds, how many the report lists

episodes.new_bonds_what: bonds first issued in those quarters
episodes.why: Recall rises because reading is the only way to see a new bond. Precision falls because a system that adds things adds some wrong things.

additions.total_what: bonds the tracker added, in the quarters whose report itemises its bonds
additions.diagnosis_by: Claude's reading of each one after scoring — a judgment, labelled as such in the author's own figure

segments.label: in the report
segments.what: the new bonds it was built to find

segments.label: existing notes
segments.what: read from a prospectus as if new

segments.label: launch notices
segments.what: no coupon yet, so not merged with the priced bond that follows

segments.label: bank options
segments.what: "up to an additional $45 million" read as a bond of its own

segments.label: misreads
segments.what: no kind, and no defect id — the source gives none

additions.legend_note: The author's figure legends four of the five segments; the two misreads are named only in its footnote and carry no defect id. The reel draws all five and names the fifth.
additions.fix_where: All three kinds are fixes to the merge step, logged for week 6 and not fixed against this run.

timing._: the one bug found by the first run and fixed before the second — both runs are reported
timing.what: The window runs up to the day the target report is filed, weeks after the quarter ends, and the engine applied everything in it. Bonds sold after the quarter ended landed in that quarter's ledger.
timing.design: The design keeps the ledger by settlement date.
timing.fix: Only events filed by the quarter end are applied.
timing.fixed_on: development data, re-run from the saved readings
timing.unchanged: Recall and new bonds caught were the same in both runs.
timing.residual: Filing date still stands in for settlement date until settlement dates are parsed, so a bond priced in the last days of a quarter can still land on the wrong side.

fresh.drawn_how: Each set drawn and labelled before the run it scores.

triage.small: Fifteen positives is still a small check: one miss would have been 93%, below the line.

new_weaknesses.what: a tender for shares read as a debt tender
a share term sheet that mentions notes

reader.b2_caveat: B2 reads more numbers, and reports 15 instruments that are not in the filings — and not one of its numbers has a sentence behind it.

disagreement.what: a total tagged in a way the key does not read

key.draw_note: Only 2 of the 25 companies had never been hand-checked, so the draw had to be extended: three of the five reports are from companies checked before, in other quarters.

truthcheck._: who produced the labels, the truth and the diagnosis — not a person
truthcheck.labeller_note: a different model from the one being tested, but not a person
truthcheck.covers: the triage labels, the reader truth, the hand-check transcriptions and the diagnosis of the 26 wrong additions
truthcheck.written_when: sets were drawn by seed before reading, and labels and truth were written and hashed before the runs
